messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Rerank model fit validation - initial results & next steps

Hi Sarah (and team),

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the search & recommendations pipeline. Per our discussion, I ran the initial rerank evaluations on your sample production logs (50k queries) and attached the NDCG/MRR export. High-level takeaways: 

- Model recommendations: rerank-small-v2 (3.6B, distilled) for latency-sensitive routes; rerank-base-quant (6B, 4-bit quant) for higher-quality routes where you can tolerate +20ms.
- NDCG@10 uplift: +8.2% absolute vs your current heuristic baseline (see ndcg_mrr_results_v1.csv). MRR improved by +0.11.
- Quality caveat: we observed a small class of queries (~4%) with title-sensitive relevance where the larger model keeps edge. We flagged those in prompt_set_v2.jsonl.

Recommended next steps (proposal):
1) Run a 2-week A/B test: 10% traffic -> rerank-small-v2, 40% traffic -> rerank-base-quant, 50% control. Collect NDCG@10, MRR, and CTR by cohort.
2) Share prompt set and failure cases with your search team; run targeted evals for title-sensitive queries.
3) If regression risk is acceptable, plan a phased rollout with canary to 20% then 100% after 2 successful checkpoints.

Attachments: ndcg_mrr_results_v1.csv, prompt_set_v2.jsonl. I've also put a draft A/B plan in rerank_ab_plan.pdf.

Questions for you: does a 2-week A/B window align with how you collect metrics? Any compliance or tagging work required on our end to pass IDs?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: ndcg_mrr_results_v1.csv] [Attachment: prompt_set_v2.jsonl]

Hey Sarah — quick note with the examples and eval detail you requested. See short failure examples below (from prompt_set_v2.jsonl):

--- example id: 87322 ---
query: "wireless headphones with long battery life"
results: heuristic ranked item X at top but user relevance favored item Y due to model understanding of "battery life" in spec sheet.
issue: title/spec mismatch; larger model keeps Y higher.

--- example id: 87401 ---
query: "best running shoes for plantar fasciitis"
results: long-form reviews ranked higher for larger model; heuristic favored recency.
issue: long-tail medical/condition phrasing where semantics matter.

Evaluation notes: we ran full evals on both rerank-small-v2 and rerank-base-quant. Summary lines from ndcg_mrr_results_v1.csv: 
- control_ndcg@10: 0.541
- rerank-small-v2_ndcg@10: 0.623
- rerank-base-quant_ndcg@10: 0.623
- control_mrr: 0.412
- rerank_small_mrr: 0.522
- rerank_base_quant_mrr: 0.523

On instrumentation: we can emit click_id and an experiment_id header on responses. For conversions, as long as you can map click_id -> conversion event in analytics, we will surface the aggregated metrics. We will add the mapping table to rerank_ab_plan.pdf.

If you want, we can also run a short focused eval on the flagged ~4% to see if prompt engineering bridges the gap before A/B.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
